arxiv-2205-08192.title: Moral reinforcement learning using actual causation
arxiv-2205-08192.creator: 1 st Tue Herlau
arxiv-2205-08192.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by 1 st Tue Herlau. Reinforcement learning systems will to a greater and greater extent make decisions that significantly impact the well-being of humans, and it is therefore essential that these systems make decisions that conform to our expectations of morally good behavior. The morally good is often defined in causal terms, as in whether one’s actions have in fact caused a particular outcome, and whether the outcome could have been anticipated.

arxiv-2305-02670.description: Abstract We investigate the multipartite entanglement of a uniformly curved quantum 3 ​ D 3D space region with boundary, realised in terms of spin networks defined on a graph with non trivial S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) SU(2) holonomies, in the framework of loop quantum gravity.

arxiv-2306-09579.title: MedFMC: A Real-world Dataset and Benchmark For Foundation Model Adaptation in Medical Image Classification
arxiv-2306-09579.creator: Dequan Wang, Xiaosong Wang, Lilong Wang, Mengzhang Li, Qian Da, Xiaoqiang Liu, Xiangyu Gao, Jun Shen, Junjun He, Tian Shen, Qi Duan, Jie Zhao, Kang Li, Yu Qiao, Shaoting Zhang
arxiv-2306-09579.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Dequan Wang, Xiaosong Wang, Lilong Wang, Mengzhang Li, Qian Da, Xiaoqiang Liu, Xiangyu Gao, Jun Shen, Junjun He, Tian Shen, Qi Duan, Jie Zhao, Kang Li, Yu Qiao, Shaoting Zhang. Foundation models, often pre-trained with large-scale data, have achieved paramount success in jump-starting various vision and language applications. Recent advances further enable adapting foundation models in downstream tasks efficiently using only a few training samples, e.g., in-context learning.

arxiv-2306-16197.title: Multi-IMU with Online Self-Consistency for Freehand 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction
arxiv-2306-16197.creator: Mingyuan Luo, Xin Yang 0, Zhongnuo Yan, Junyu Li, Yuanji Zhang, Jiongquan Chen, Xindi Hu, Jikuan Qian, Jun Cheng, Dong Ni (✉)
arxiv-2306-16197.description: Abstract Ultrasound (US) imaging is a popular tool in clinical diagnosis, offering safety, repeatability, and real-time capabilities. Freehand 3D US is a technique that provides a deeper understanding of scanned regions without increasing complexity. However, estimating elevation displacement and accumulation error remains challenging, making it difficult to infer the relative position using images alone.

arxiv-2505-02434.title: Early evolution of super-Eddington accretion flow in tidal disruption events 2023 Early evolution of super-Eddington accretion flow in tidal disruption events – 15
arxiv-2505-02434.creator: Erlin Qiao, Yongxin Wu, Yiyang Lin, Meng Guo, Jifeng Liu, Chenlei Guo, Chichuan Jin, Ning Jiang
arxiv-2505-02434.description: Abstract Tidal disruption events (TDEs) are luminous black hole (BH) transient sources, which are detected mainly in X-ray and optical bands. It is generally believed that the X-ray emission in TDEs is produced by an accretion disc formed as the stellar debris accreted onto the central BH.

pmc-11414209.title: Knowledge, attitude and practice toward to artificial intelligent patient-controlled analgesia among anesthesiologists: a cross-sectional study in east China’s Jiangsu Province
pmc-11414209.creator: Jiaqin Cai, Shiyi Huang, Yueyi Jiang, Yihu Zhou, Lin Zhang, Lianbing Gu, Jing Tan
pmc-11414209.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundInadequate postoperative analgesia greatly affects the recovery of patients, can poses a substantial health and economic burden. Patient-controlled analgesia is the most commonly used method for postoperative pain relief. However, the situation of inadequate analgesia still exists. Artificial intelligent Patient-controlled analgesia (Ai-PCA) system can make it easier for medical staff to understand the pain level of patients in order to deal with it in time.

pmc-12528747.title: Microglia-specific regulation of lipid metabolism in Alzheimer’s disease revealed by microglial depletion in 5xFAD Mice
pmc-12528747.creator: Ziying Xu, Sepideh Kiani Shabestari, Savannah Barannikov, Kevin F Bieniek, Mathew Blurton-Jones, Juan Pablo Palavicini, Xianlin Han
pmc-12528747.description: Abnormal lipid metabolism is observed in Alzheimer’s disease (AD), but its contribution to disease progression remains unclear. Genetic studies indicate that microglia, the brain’s resident immune cells, influence lipid processing during AD. Here, we show that microglia—the brain’s resident immune cells—selectively regulate lipid accumulation that associated with disease pathology in both AD mouse models and human postmortem brains.

pmc-13092326.title: Surface Structure of Polar Silver Iodide (0001) in Various Liquids: No Indication for a Surface Reconstruction
pmc-13092326.creator: Kim Noelle Dreier, Annamaria Latus, Ralf Bechstein, Angelika Kühnle
pmc-13092326.description: Silver iodide (AgI) has long been known as a material that induces precipitation in clouds. The superior ice nucleation ability is commonly explained by the close lattice match between β‐AgI(0001) and the basal plane of ice. However, this surface is polar, indicating that a stabilization mechanism should be present.

pmc-13263975.description: Background and ObjectiveMetabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the leading cause of chronic liver disease, affecting approximately 30 percent of the population worldwide. pmc-13567039.title: Design, Synthesis and Anticancer Evaluation of Novel SO2F-Containing Medicinally Privileged Structures via Ketone-Directed C–H Functionalization
pmc-13567039.creator: Seungwan Kim, Lingayya Rajaka, Saegun Kim, In Jae Bang, Hyun Woo Lee, Minseo Choi, Jihyo Lee, Myunghwa Jung, Hyosik Woo, Sangil Han, Ki Yong Lee, Hyun Jin Kim, Ha Ryong Kim, Sang Hoon Han
pmc-13567039.description: The weakly coordinating ketone group-directed C–H functionalizations of chromones, flavones, 1,4-naphthoquinones, (thio)xanthones, and acridones with ethenesulfonyl fluoride under rhodium(III) or ruthenium(II) catalysis are described. pmc-13613406.title: Synergistic Heterojunction and Noble-Metal Sensitization in Ag/In2O3/CuO for Enhanced Triethylamine Sensing with Trace Detection Capability
pmc-13613406.creator: Ruidong Xiong, Min Wang, Shuhao Jiang, Lei Liu, Yan Yang, Jie Zheng, Yingkai Liu
pmc-13613406.description: Triethylamine (TEA) poses a serious threat to human health, necessitating high-performance gas sensors. This work enhances TEA sensing by co-modifying In2O3 with CuO and Ag. A series of In2O3-based composites (binary In2O3/CuO with different ratios of In to Cu, and ternary Ag/In2O3/CuO with 3–9 wt % Ag) was prepared via solvothermal calcination and chemical reduction.
